description: Family-skewed cruise passenger composition for the NORO-AGE-FOOD-01 demographic arms. Paired with a ship_graph.agent_classes override that raises the passenger_family share to 0.25, it puts ~20% of passengers under 18 — the child share a family-market hull actually carries (the shipped 0.10 family fraction cannot reach it: 0.10 x 0.56 = 5.6% of passengers at these weights).

published_inputs: No measured family-market cruise age composition is in the repository; the under-18 share target (~20% of passengers) is the design's declared arm coordinate, stated here so the weights are transparent.
steps: passenger_family splits its child draw across the two child bands (0-4 and 5-17) rather than the single 'child' label — a family hull carries infants as well as school-age children; both bands read the same 0.51 presentation factor on norwalk_gi, so the split is honest composition, not a mechanism dodge.
Weights {0-4: 0.12, 5-17: 0.44, young_adult: 0.20, adult: 0.24} put 0.56 of the family class under 18 and keep the remaining 0.44 in the parent bands (18-34 / 35-49).

passenger_general, passenger_elderly and all crew classes keep the repository default bundle's band lists verbatim — only the family class's age draw changes; the class-share shift lives in the tier's ship_graph.agent_classes override, not here.
refusals: All weights in this bundle are Grade C declared — no source measures the age composition of a family-market cruise at publishable grade in-tree, and the arm's purpose is to bracket the demographic axis, not to claim a measured hull.

Composite passenger composition under the arm's class fractions (general 0.35 / family 0.25 / elderly 0.10 of a 0.70 passenger share): ~20% of passengers under 18, ~14% >=65 — versus ~5% and ~14% on the default bundle.
